claims.text: Reducing FeMnNiGeSi alloys to nanoscale films or nanoribbons alters interfacial strain and introduces edge effects.
The altered interfacial strain and edge effects increase magnetic domain-wall pinning.
Nanoscale interfacial and edge effects increase local thermal gradients.
The modified nanoscale microstructure reduces effective magnetocaloric amplitude relative to bulk FeMnNiGeSi forms.
The modified nanoscale microstructure increases hysteresis during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles relative to bulk forms.
As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi films and nanoribbons exhibit intrinsic nanoscale heterogeneity, substrate-induced strain, and edge confinement.
Changing the substrate lattice parameter or underlayer lattice mismatch changes the local strain state at the film interface.
Reducing interfacial strain produces fewer or less effective domain-wall pinning sites.
Reducing interfacial strain produces more homogeneous thermal gradients.
Reduced domain-wall pinning allows magnetic domains to reorient more readily under an applied field.
Greater domain mobility enhances the magnetocaloric response.
Localized thermal lags caused by limited heat transfer contribute to increased hysteresis and suppressed magnetocaloric amplitude.
Relieving or tailoring interfacial strain will increase magnetocaloric amplitude relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Relieving or tailoring interfacial strain will reduce hysteresis relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Improved interfacial heat transfer will permit faster cooling-cycle frequencies without compromising performance.
The proposed mechanism applies at applied magnetic fields below 200 mT.
The proposed mechanism applies to film thicknesses or nanoribbon widths below approximately 100 nm.
The strain-mediated mechanism is expected to be less relevant for thicker films or at higher applied fields.
